blocks.prompt: 11. The trajectories of two projectiles in a physics experiment are modeled by the homogeneous equation \(9x^{2} - 12xy + 4y^{2} = 0\). Prove that this represents two coincident lines and find angle between them.
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal ke do hisse hain: pehle saabit karna ke lines coincident hain, phir un ke darmiyan angle batana.
Projectiles ke raaste yahan seedhi lines maane gaye hain; coincident ka matlab dono raaste bilkul ek jaise.
Rule: Theorem 8 mein \(h^{2} = ab\) ho to lines coincident, aur angle formula mein numerator zero ho jata hai.
Plan: \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhna, \(h^{2} - ab = 0\) dikhana, perfect square se woh line nikalna, phir angle.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(9x^{2} - 12xy + 4y^{2} = 0\).
Saabit karna: lines coincident hain. Maloom karna: un ke darmiyan angle.
Tareeqa: Theorem 8 (coincident agar \(h^{2} = ab\)) aur \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\).

\(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhein
\[a = 9,\quad 2h = -12 \Rightarrow h = -6,\quad b = 4\]
Kyun: \(h\) \(xy\) ke coefficient ka aadha hai, sign ke saath.

\(h^{2} - ab\) ka test
\[h^{2} - ab = 36 - 36 = 0\]
Kyun: \((-6)^{2} = 36\) aur \(9 \times 4 = 36\). Barabar hain, yani Theorem 8 ka coincident case.
Dhyan dein: \((-6)^{2}\) positive 36 hai, \(-36\) nahi.

Woh ek line
\[9x^{2} - 12xy + 4y^{2} = (3x - 2y)^{2} = 0\]
\[3x - 2y = 0 \text{ (do dafa)}\]
Kyun: \(p^{2} - 2pq + q^{2} = (p - q)^{2}\), jahan \(p = 3x\) aur \(q = 2y\); \(2pq = 12xy\). Dono factors ek jaise, to dono raaste ek hi line par.

Angle
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{0}}{9 + 4} = 0\]
\[\theta = 0^{\circ}\]
Kyun: lines ek doosre ke upar hain, un ke beech koi khulaav (opening) nahi, is liye angle zero. Answer key bhi \(0^{\circ}\) deti hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[(3x - 2y)^{2} = 9x^{2} - 12xy + 4y^{2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: square khola to di gayi equation wapas aa gayi; saboot pakka.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(h^{2} = ab\), is liye dono lines \(3x - 2y = 0\) hain (coincident); angle \(= 0^{\circ}\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein is sawal ka jawab number 12 par ('\(0^{\circ}\)') chhapa hai, jo sahi hai; sirf numbering ek aage khiski hui hai.
